$comment: OMN-18798. The vocabulary of a destructive git command this guard refuses
when the command's effective git root is the REGISTRY CLONE at $OMNI_HOME
itself, and the sanctioned alternatives it points a caller at.
Read by plugins/onex/hooks/lib/shared_tree_git_guard.py, which is invoked
by the pre_tool_use_shared_tree_git_guard.sh PreToolUse hook. The
vocabulary lives here, not in the checker, matching the OMN-17334
git-stash policy this file is patterned on: adding a shape is a config
edit visible in one place rather than a rule a reader has to infer from a
Python literal.
Why this exists
The registry clone at $OMNI_HOME is the ONE repository in the fleet where
many concurrent agent
lanes work in the SAME working tree (docs/tracking/, docs/workflows/,
.claude/workflows/, scripts/). Code repos use per-ticket worktrees and do
not have this problem. Two measured failure classes:
1. DESTRUCTION. `git reflog` recorded 20 `reset: moving to origin/main`
entries in the shared clone on 2026-09-18 alone. Those resets twice
re-orphaned a staged 1.9 MB ledger-roll archive holding 1,258
append-only coordination rows, leaving them untracked on one disk
with no copy in any commit, on any branch, on any remote, for 2h22m;
a `git clean -fd` in that window would have destroyed them and left
origin/main showing a ledger that had never lost them. The same
verbs twice dropped a peer lane's unpushed commit from local main
and twice reverted a peer lane's uncommitted edit (OMN-18798,
the registry repo pull requests 407 and 408).
2. STRANDING, which destroys nothing and is quieter. A feature branch
checked out in the shared clone makes commit_lock.py refuse EVERY
other lane's ledger commit with exit 78, STRANDED CLONE, for as long
as it stays checked out. Measured by lane
dev-lane-broker-recreate-on-warm-deploy-diag-0125: three rows
appended at 01:24Z reached a committed copy only at 11:17Z, and the
refusals at 02:37:19Z and 02:37:41Z named the branch. The only
signal is an exit code on somebody else's terminal. This is why
`git checkout -b` and `git switch -c` are refused here and not only
the destructive verbs.
Doctrine: the workspace CLAUDE.md Operating Rule 19, whose closing
paragraph (landed as registry pull request 410) states the prohibition
this guard mechanises.
Rule 19 was doctrine-only until this ticket.
refused_subcommands -- the git subcommands this guard evaluates when the
effective git root IS the registry clone. `reset`, `switch`, `clean` and
`rebase` are refused in every form. `checkout` and `branch` carry their
own refinement below, because each has a sanctioned shape.
checkout: refused EXCEPT the path-scoped restore recipe Operating Rule 17
sanctions -- `git checkout -- <path>` and `git checkout <ref> -- <path>`
-- which touches only the named paths and no shared state. Three
exceptions to the exception: a `-b`/`-B` branch creation is refused even
with a `--` (it is the stranding shape); a path operand naming the whole
tree (blanket_path_operands) is refused because it is a blanket checkout
wearing path-scoped syntax, which is the verb Rule 19 names; and a
checkout with operands but NO `--` separator is refused because git
itself cannot tell a ref from a path there, so neither can this guard --
fail closed and use the explicit form. A bare `git checkout` with no
operands changes nothing and is not refused.
merge: refused UNLESS the invocation carries one of merge_allowed_flags.
`--ff-only` is the sanctioned sync verb: it either advances the pointer
or refuses, and it never runs a content merge, so it cannot resolve a
peer lane's rows away. A merge WITHOUT it can, and did: on 2026-09-19
at 14:52:55Z a lane merged origin/main into a feature branch checked out
in the shared clone with the ort strategy, and the round trip back to
`main` at 14:55:04Z did not carry rows appended between 14:48Z and
14:53Z. `--abort`, `--quit` and `--continue` are allowed because they
manage a merge that is ALREADY in progress -- refusing them would strand
the tree mid-conflict, which is worse than the state the guard is
protecting.
branch: only the shapes that move the tree out from under peer lanes are
refused -- a delete or a rename (branch_destructive_flags) whose target
IS the currently checked-out branch, read from .git/HEAD rather than by
running git. `git branch -d <some-other-branch>` and `git branch <name>`
do not change the working tree and are not refused. An unreadable HEAD
fails closed.
allowed_always -- recorded for the reader, NOT consulted by the checker.
These shapes are allowed because they are not in refused_subcommands at
all, which is the stronger statement: there is no allowlist to fall out
of date. `git merge --ff-only`, `git fetch`, `git pull --ff-only`, and
every read (status, log, diff, show, rev-parse, reflog, worktree list)
never match the refused vocabulary.
registry_root_envs / registry_root_markers -- how the registry clone is
identified. The env vars are tried first, in order. The markers are the
fallback so the guard does not go DARK when the environment is thin: a
hook process with no OMNI_HOME would otherwise admit every refused verb
in the exact tree this guard exists to protect. A directory matches only
when it is a git root AND carries every marker.
Scope, stated so it is not over-read: this guard fires ONLY when the
effective git root is the registry clone itself. A worktree under
omni_worktrees/ has its own .git file and its own root, so it is never
matched; neither is a code-repo canonical clone under $OMNI_HOME, whose
root is $OMNI_HOME/<repo> and not $OMNI_HOME. Those surfaces already have
the OMN-7018/OMN-14330 worktree guard.
There is deliberately NO escape entry -- no consent citation, no wildcard
shape, no exempt marker. Every refused verb has a sanctioned alternative
that reaches the same outcome without touching state a peer lane owns, so
there is nothing a legitimate use needs that this guard blocks.
Deliberately NOT refused, and named rather than left silent: `git restore`
and `git restore --staged`, which can be as blanket as a checkout. They
are outside the verb set this ticket's brief enumerated, and adding a verb
nobody measured is how a guard starts refusing work it was never shown to
protect. Add it when a collision is measured, with the measurement.
safe_alternatives: do the work in a worktree under $OMNI_HOME/omni_worktrees/<ticket>/<repo> instead of the shared clone; sync only by fast-forward, git -C $OMNI_HOME merge --ff-only origin/main, and only when the clone carries no unpushed commits; or restore individual files with a path-scoped git checkout <ref> -- <path> naming each path
